source.stem:
The diagram shows the only three forces acting on an object.
What is the resultant force on the object?

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: applied force is the same as its neighbouring term in this chapter, so the decision does not change.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The decision still holds even if we ignore this condition: Apply this to objects at rest and to objects already moving.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: change in state of motion, direction, speed, shape, or a combination of effects happens first, and that produces applied force.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: This rule applies even when Apply this to objects at rest and to objects already moving is not true.

intelligence.enrichment: A force applied on an object may make it move from rest, change its speed, change its direction of motion, change its shape, or cause several of these effects together. applied force -> change in state of motion, direction, speed, shape, or a combination of effects The learner correctly applies this rule: A force applied on an object may make it move from rest, change its speed, change its direction of motion, change its shape, or cause several of these effects together. A force only counts when an object starts moving from rest.
